title: Rain Check
caption: Spoken word over slow film noir jazz. A deep, weary male voice speaks, not sings, a hard-boiled detective's monologue in English, dry and unhurried, close to the microphone, with long pauses. Behind him a smoky tenor saxophone, soft brushed drums, a slow walking upright bass and sparse late-night piano chords, the hush of rain. Cynical, tired, a private eye alone in his office after midnight. Intimate vintage studio sound.
lyrics:
[Intro - Saxophone]

[Spoken Word]
It was raining the night she walked in.
It's always raining the night they walk in.
She had a photograph, an envelope, and a story.
The photograph was real. The envelope was thick.
The story had more holes than my umbrella.

[Spoken Word]
I took the case. I always take the case.
Rent's due on the first,
and the first doesn't care who's lying to who.

[Instrumental Break - Saxophone]

[Spoken Word]
Three days. Two bars. One black sedan,
parked where a black sedan had no business being.
A man in a good suit told me to forget her name.
I told him I was never good with names.
He wasn't good with jokes.

[Spoken Word]
By Thursday I knew where the husband was.
By Friday I knew why she never wanted him found.
In this town the truth is like the last train.
You either catch it, or you walk home in the rain.

[Instrumental Break - Piano]

[Spoken Word]
She paid me in cash and didn't count it.
I didn't count it either.
Some things you'd rather not know the price of.

[Spoken Word]
The rain stopped around four.
It'll be back.
It always comes back.

[Outro - Saxophone]
